original_card.question: Can one unresolved retention, output-consumer, hosting or physical-cost obligation complete a pinned QQ16 controller proposal within budget?
methods: Design and price one consumer or retained-state boundary for a pinned local decoder, including final restoration.
Audit one claimed physical invoice or prove a target-specific obstruction for its explicit retention/hosting contract.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed premise of the fixed F0/B1 observation obstruction. Show exactly which query is recovered, legal native reads and restoration, and a full favorable budget including cover maps, helpers and endpoints. Local inverse identities alone do not close the global controller. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the QQ16 row in research-family-status.md. The fixed-first-pair witness remains scoped; pending #2540 adds early records and claims a complete local native decoder, but not a favorable global controller. Read its output-frame and ownership contract before designing another inverse.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only. Read the named package and review before relying on its local evidence; this command is not its replay or supplier admission.

original_card.first_experiment: Check live claims and pin the newest relevant completed local word (starting lead #2540). Choose one unresolved consumer, retention, whole-cover movement, hosting or precision obligation. Price the complete proposal and test that obligation; do not repeat its claimed local inverse or native reconstruction unless providing distinct independent verification.
original_card.bottleneck_link: The native local words exist; retained query information and its physical access are the missing link to a composed recursive interface.
allowed_variations: One paid query, one changed first pair, or one precisely specified affine helper state.
A counterexample or lower bound for that exact proposed repair.
One unresolved obligation of a newer local decoder, with exact source heads and a distinct claim/domain.

Treating cover-map counts as zero-cost physical address operations.
Recreating the pending complete local decoder or early-record/output-bank coalescing already under investigation without a distinct audit or changed premise.

actual_scope: Price the retention obligation itself: in the PR1664 scalar common-frame transport model, what paid mass does an array retained across calls force (storage versus frame catch-up), with the consumer level and the consumer's observation contract explicit; then apply it to the two #1166 c18956869 routes (the QQ16 INIT64+d_A final-record contract in both published variants; gap-1 shared-source centre sharing) and clarify the retention row of the QQ16 retained caller #2540/#2651.
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether one unresolved retention/consumer/hosting obligation can complete a pinned QQ16 controller proposal. The live blocker was a pricing question, not a construction: #1166 c18956869 asked maintainers which retention convention (S) or (C) applies, and three routes (two in #1166, the #2540 caller row in #2617) depend on it. We derive the transport-model price instead of assuming a convention. Physical storage remains outside the moment and is recorded as UNKNOWN; no supplier is attempted.
bottleneck_link: Retained query information is the QQ16 family's missing link to a composed recursive interface. This result fixes the moment price of that retention (frame catch-up: 8 coordinates per level advanced per record row independent of what the consumer's contract may combine). Under the stated observation contract with final-value reads (P_obs), P_rank with uncompressed delivery (our reading of the contract), P4, the stated capture times and current-frame consumers satisfying the decoder-timing premise P_dec (each bank's decoder uses an observation that exists only after its pair's last local call, as the derived decoders do), it rejects the INIT64+d_A final-record route in both published variants: 3648 / 3456 units per replica with the stated end decoder, at least 2496 / 2304 when each bank decodes as soon as its observed field is final (P_Y), and at least 1344 / 1152 for every timing at or after each bank's last local call (P_early); all exceed the exact 896 no-saving threshold. Bank 0's INIT via f0 lowers each by 128 and changes no verdict. P_dec is load-bearing: at decoders right after their own last captures the moment bound drops to 512 (kappa cap 0.0020286, above the selected kappa; no decoder is known to run there). The P_early value also depends on the stated capture times: an AI review pass found that captures one level later with an extra read of the transient Y give 832 / 640 at P_early (below 896, caps still below the selected kappa), while P_final and P_Y stay >= 896. Without P_rank, Theorem B (#2074) still rejects at the end decoder (1952 / 1824); at multi-level timings it needs an own-bank premise (1344 / 1216 at P_Y, both >= 896; 800 / 608 at P_early, below the selected kappa) and its count alone does not decide there except, for independent captures, the original variant at P_Y (deliveries of 608 / 544 and 112 / 0 meet it; 608 is below the selected kappa). It finds no moment gain for gap-1 centre sharing under its premises (the f0->f2 information question stays open), and clarifies that the #2540-style caller's retention row is its existing 16 H8, one charge. The remaining levers (late capture of INIT information, endpoint reads at the consumer frame, compression before the climb, physical storage) all lie in the observation contract or outside the moment.
stop_rule: Stop if the frame-model search falsifies the min-cut, or a legal synchronization without paid mass appears (publish a parametrized price as a handoff instead). Otherwise stop after the package, the posts and one audit PR. No per-record-class schedule search; no census extensions.
evidence: Written proofs (PROOF.md: Lemma 1 restated from PR1664, Lemma 2 storage neutrality, Proposition 3 exact both-direction meeting-level minimum, Corollary 4 eight coordinates per level, Proposition 5 S/C versus the law, with lagging-pair records shown not to separate the law from (C); section 7.2 per-cut application of Theorem B, valid alone for one consumer level, and the own-bank per-cut additivity proof under its strong reading). Finite exact checks: verify.py (pinned template levels and bridge levels, last writes of X_(k,U), two-sided hosting at 21 route instants in replica 0, controls, both route variants at three consumer timings, Theorem B floors, pinned ceiling.py pricing including the PRICE-GATE.json storage ceiling and PR2470's centre-like limit, 34,454 + 4,044 frame-model instances by BFS on complete domains, rational tensor toy, the decoder-timing counterexample 512 / 640, bank 0's INIT via f0, per-term revival masses, 17 negative controls with asserted failure messages) and independent_check.py (coordinate-set replay of a byte-identical template copy from a second pinned archive, Theorem B by split enumeration, per-family hosted height replay of all 16 replicas (12 instants under both equal-time conventions, the 9 time-88 and all-initial instants after their time settles), Decimal-80 moments, echelon Dijkstra on 2,432 instances, 2 controls rejected for their stated reasons). Premises are explicit and unproved here: P_obs (the QQ16 observation contract), P_rank (finite-model evidence only; uncompressed delivery is our reading of the published contract), the stated capture times, consumer timing (P_final stated; P_Y a lower bound under the final-value read convention; P_early a lower bound under P_dec, a property of the derived decoders), P4, PR2540's rho = 16 (PR2511), Theorem B (unreviewed) and, for its multi-level rows, our own-bank premise. P_glob is used only for zero costs and count-only deliveries. Physical storage is UNKNOWN. No human or formal-kernel review; review so far consists of AI passes in the same automated loop.

open_questions.question: Can the INIT information be captured later, or read at the consumer frame, under a priced observation contract?
open_questions.why_it_matters: INIT64's catch-up is the binding term of both published variants (1,920 units per replica at P_Y, 1,152 at P_early). At the end decoder no INIT lever suffices (d_A alone 960; all-initial reads alone 768, cap below the selected kappa); at P_Y the original variant's d_A term alone (576) loses to PR2474; the live target is the all-initial variant at P_Y, whose reads cost 384 and leave at most 189 units (vs PR2474) or 195 (vs the selected record) for the INIT information. Bank 0's INIT via f0 (saving 128) is a first instance; endpoint reads at the consumer frame pay no catch-up in the moment.
open_questions.first_step: For each bank, find the latest cut at which the initial query information can still be rebuilt from rows a contract may read, and price that read both with Corollary 4 and as a read contract.
open_questions.blocked_by: No priced observation contract for endpoint or ordinary reads; P_rank is finite-model evidence only.

open_questions.question: Do the forward query histories f2, f4, f6, f8 used by the derived final-record decoders add retention catch-up?
open_questions.why_it_matters: They are absent from the 464 array-call count; retained as one 8-row array each, they would add 768 (output-level capture) to 1,024 (input-level capture) units under an end decoder, 384 to 640 at P_Y, or 0 to 256 at P_early (f2, f4, f6 alone: 768-960, 384-576, 0-192).
open_questions.first_step: Identify whether the QQ16 words keep the forward histories in data ports or in separate arrays, then apply Corollary 4.
open_questions.blocked_by: The storage location of the histories in a complete controller is not specified.

open_questions.question: What does physical storage of the sixteen early arrays across B1 cost for the #2540/#2651 caller?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the only cost that could make the retained caller preferable to zero-retention #2707, whose surplus (192 wrappers, 256 maps, 8,368 scalars) is also outside the moment.
open_questions.first_step: Bind the sixteen arrays of #2651 to concrete streams and tape positions across B1 and compare with #2707's surplus in one physical cost model.
open_questions.blocked_by: No maintainer-accepted physical storage/tape price for new arrays; the moment cannot supply it (Lemma 2).

open_questions.question: Which consumer, in which frame, accepts the 224 F_U1 outputs of #2540/#2707?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Proposition 3 needs the consumer level as a premise; a different consumer frame changes the catch-up from record climb to partner descent.
open_questions.first_step: Determine from pinned sources whether any caller contract names the frame of the next consumer (handoff thread #2657).
open_questions.blocked_by: No complete caller contract for the QQ16 decoder outputs is published.

open_questions.question: Can idle sweeps be re-timed so that retained records sit in zero-advance windows?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The law is zero while the source pair advances no level (pair 3 across six calls); restoration deferral is mass-neutral (PR1012), so window placement is a genuine design lever.
open_questions.first_step: For one route, list the records' source pairs and the idle sweeps that separate capture from consumption, and test one re-timing on the level timeline.
open_questions.blocked_by: Re-timing must preserve hosting windows and the selected endpoint contract; not attempted in this session.
